facts.big: He told me that it was a mistake
facts.label: Contar o que alguém disse
facts.sub: Use told me that ou said that + passado: He told me that it was a mistake. She said that the machine was not working.

facts.label: Me disse que…
facts.sub: Use told + pessoa + that + frase no passado: He told me that it was a mistake. Depois de told, sempre há uma pessoa: me, her, us. That pode ser omitido na fala.

facts.label: Disse que…
facts.sub: Use said + that + frase no passado: She said that the machine was not working. Said não leva pessoa direta. Para a pessoa, use said to me, ou prefira told me.

compare.ask: He told me that it was a mistake.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “ele me disse que foi um erro”.
compare.tip: Diga: “He told me that it was a mistake.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use told + pessoa + that, ou said that. O verbo depois costuma ir ao passado: He told me that it was a mistake. He said that the machine was not working.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: He told me that it was a mistake.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Told is used with a person: told me.
Said is often used without me.

items.why: We say He told me that… or He said that…

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Told is used with a person: told me. → Verdadeiro (He told me that…)
Said is often used without me. → Verdadeiro (She said that…)
We say “He said me that…” → Falso (We say He told me that… or He said that…)

pages.title: A store in Denver · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cloudy Monday in Denver. Olivia checks her receipt at home. She sees the same amount two times. She goes back to the store to ask about it. Pam is the manager and listens with care. Olivia wants her money back.

“Hello, Olivia. You look worried. What’s the problem?” says Pam. “The receipt says I paid twice. The cashier told me that it was a mistake.” says Olivia. “I’m sorry. When did you buy the things?” says Pam.
